overclaims: A Stanford study from May 2024 found that commercial legal AI tools sold as hallucination-free still gave wrong answers 17% to 34% of the time.
The evidence shows the problems persisted; it does not measure how much they improved.
checks.note: The Stanford findings are more than 17% and more than 34%, not a bounded 17–34% range. Specify the study's legal-query benchmark and that hallucinations include unsupported citations. The final limitation is too categorical: e4 reports a 40% higher score on OpenAI's internal adversarial factuality evaluations, although that does not quantify overall improvement.
